w:r.w:t: A System and Method for Privacy-Preserving Real-Time Multi-Threat Detection
Using a Cascaded Neural Processing Unit Pipeline on an Edge Computing Platform

A privacy-preserving edge-AI home security system comprising a single-board edge computing host operatively coupled via PCIe to a neural processing unit, hosting a three-stage cascaded inference pipeline in which (i) a primary INT8 object detector identifies domestic threats at 52.2 FPS, (ii) a secondary binary classifier verifies weapon crops from tight bounding-box regions, and (iii) a depth-variance pre-filter flags flat-surface presentation candidates — all three stages sharing one NPU virtual device. An asynchronous, CPU-core-pinned, bounded-queue architecture structurally isolates the inference path from concurrent web, voice, authentication, and logging services, sustaining 52.26 ± 0.76 FPS across all operating modes at 5.89 W mean board power. A mode-gated alert engine with on-device Gaussian privacy blur, AES-256-CBC encrypted evidence capture, and authenticated remote access ensures no raw video leaves the device. The system achieves mAP@0.5 = 0.854 for four-class threat detection in INT8 deployment on a USD 411 hardware platform.

The present invention relates to edge-computing systems for real-time visual threat detection. More specifically, it relates to a hardware-software co-designed platform that deploys a cascaded neural processing unit (NPU) pipeline — comprising a primary object detector, a secondary classifier, and a depth-variance pre-filter — on a single low-power single-board computer, without any cloud dependency, to detect domestic threats and generate encrypted, authenticated alerts in real time.

Consumer home security systems fall into two categories: (a) cloud-backed systems that stream raw video to remote data centres — forfeiting user privacy and creating data-egress risk — and (b) local single-board-computer builds limited to frame-differencing motion detection, lacking deep-learning inference, secondary verification, or encrypted evidence capture. Prior art weapon detection deployments (YOLOv4/v5/v7 on Jetson TX1, FPGA, or Raspberry Pi 4 without NPU offload) operate without a secondary verifier, depth pre-filter, privacy mode, or encrypted-evidence path. No prior art combines a multi-stage NPU cascade on one accelerator, CPU-pinned async thread isolation, on-device privacy blur, and AES-256 encrypted evidence capture within a sub-10 W single-board platform.

The invention is a privacy-first, edge-AI home security system comprising a Raspberry Pi 5 single-board computer, a Hailo-8L NPU (13 TOPS, INT8), and a cascaded inference pipeline implemented entirely on the edge device. Key measured outcomes:
52.2 FPS primary detection at 18.4 ms NPU latency.
52.26 ± 0.76 FPS sustained across all operating modes under full concurrent CPU-side load.
mAP@0.5 = 0.854 for four-class domestic threat detection (INT8 deployment).
5.89 W mean board power under full inference + service load.
Zero raw video egress — all inference, alerting, evidence capture, and streaming on-device.
A privacy-preserving real-time threat detection apparatus comprising:
A single-board edge computing host (Raspberry Pi 5) with CPU-core affinity assignment, coupled via PCIe Gen3 x1 to a dedicated NPU (Hailo-8L, 13 TOPS INT8).
A camera sensor (Sony IMX708) on CSI-2 delivering frames to a GStreamer multimedia pipeline.

A cascaded NPU inference engine comprising: (a) a primary four-class object detector (YOLOv8s INT8 HEF, 22.9 MB, 52.2 FPS); (b) a secondary Safe/Weapon binary classifier (MobileNetV2 INT8 HEF) on tight bounding-box crops; (c) a monocular depth-variance pre-filter (MiDaS Small INT8 HEF) as a flat-surface detection gate — all three sharing one HailoRT VDevice.
An asynchronous bounded-queue decoupling mechanism (capacity 2, non-blocking put_nowait, intentional drop on full) between the NPU inference thread and CPU-side services.
A CPU-core-pinned threading model: Core 0 = camera capture; Core 1 = HailoRT inference; Core 2 = secondary verifier + depth; Core 3 = OS + web services.
A mode-gated alert engine with five operating states (DND, Email-Off, Idle, Emergency, Privacy) serialised by a threading lock.
A privacy mode applying Gaussian blur (kernel 51 px, sigma 30 px) to every detected person bounding box before any frame delivery to display, stream, or subscriber.
An encrypted evidence subsystem: AES-256-CBC clip encryption with SSH (paramiko) transport to a remote store.
Acquiring frames via CSI-2 into a GStreamer pipeline on an edge computing host.
Dispatching frames over PCIe DMA to an INT8 NPU running a primary object detector — no CPU involvement during forward pass.
Applying a three-consecutive-frame gate on danger-class detections; triggering alert only after 3 consecutive confirmed frames (~57.5 ms at 52.2 FPS).

Asynchronously enqueuing tight bounding-box crops (bounded queue, capacity 2) to a secondary thread; passing crops to (a) a binary weapon classifier and (b) a monocular depth estimator; intentionally dropping crops when queue is full to protect primary inference throughput.
Classifying person crops with depth-map variance below a fixed threshold as flat-surface candidates.
Applying Gaussian privacy blur on person bounding boxes in privacy mode before output.
On confirmed danger: asynchronously fan-out to (a) WebSocket push, (b) SMTPS email with per-label 60 s cooldown, (c) AES-256-CBC encrypted clip upload via SSH — all off the inference thread.
Primary detector compiled to INT8 HEF (22.9 MB) via post-training quantisation with 128 calibration images; normalisation embedded in HEF graph. mAP@0.5 = 0.854 on held-out test split.
Three HEF models share one HailoRT VDevice via sequential time-shared infer calls; combined secondary-stage latency per crop < 4 ms.
Per-label SMTPS alert cooldown of 60 seconds prevents alert flooding on sustained detections.
Deadman watchdog polls inference heartbeat every 10 s; triggers restart after 180 s silence.
Presence monitor uses ARP scanning at 30 s intervals with 90 s grace window to detect occupant devices and switch operating modes.
Authentication: PBKDF2-SHA256 at 600,000 iterations, per-user salt, HTTP-only session cookie; admin 2FA via 6-digit OTP over SMTPS, 10-minute expiry.
Asymmetric confidence thresholds: 0.60 for Person (watch class), 0.25–0.35 for weapon classes (alert classes).
Voice assistant transcribes locally; only text transcript (never audio/video) is sent externally as a stateless JSON-constrained LLM completion when no local rule matches.
Events drained off-thread to append-only text, JSON, and SQLite store; catch-up REST endpoint /api/events?since=T without unbounded server buffering.
Mean board power under full concurrent load: 5.89 ± 1.43 W; NPU surface temperature rise: +3.8°C above ambient idle.

Every method claim must reference at least one physical hardware element (NPU, camera, PCIe bus, edge host) — no pure software claims.
Independent claims should be broad (any NPU + single-board + cascaded pipeline). Dependent claims add the specific Hailo-8L / Pi 5 / YOLOv8s details.

The System is deployed on a Raspberry Pi 5 (BCM2712, quad-core Cortex-A76, 2.8 GHz overclocked, 16 GB LPDDR4X-4267, Raspberry Pi OS Debian 12, Linux 6.12.x). A Hailo-8L AI HAT+ on the PCIe Gen3 x1 M.2 slot provides 13 TOPS INT8. Video: Raspberry Pi Camera Module v3 (Sony IMX708) via CSI-2. Storage: 1 TB SATA SSD (USB 3.0). Network: 802.11ac Wi-Fi. Total BOM: USD 411 / INR 38,085.

The pipeline extends the Hailo TAPPAS GStreamer framework. A libcamerasrc element captures frames; videoscale/videoconvert letterbox-resizes to 640x640. The pipeline forks: the inference branch dispatches to the Hailo-8L via HailoNet (NMS: IoU 0.45, confidence 0.35) in a HailoFilter; a bypass branch holds the raw frame in a queue. HailoMuxer re-aligns both. An identity element exposes the buffer to the application callback as a pad probe. HailoOverlay renders annotated output.

YOLOv8s fine-tuned on a four-class corpus (Hammer, Knife, Person, Scissors; 6,226 images, 5,311 instances) and compiled to a 22.9 MB INT8 HEF via Hailo DFC v3.33.1 (128 calibration images; normalisation embedded in HEF graph). Performance: mAP@0.5 = 0.854, mAP@0.5:0.95 = 0.682 on held-out test split (within +0.007 / +0.012 of FP32). Throughput: 52.2 FPS at 18.4 ms NPU latency. Confidence thresholds: 0.60 (Person), 0.25–0.35 (weapon classes).

Each weapon-class crop (224x224 tight bounding-box) is classified as Safe or Weapon. Fine-tuned: 5 head-only epochs + 35 full epochs (AdamW, focal loss gamma=2.0). Accuracy: 99.0% on 500-crop balanced held-out set (95% Wilson CI [97.7%, 99.6%]). Runs at 500+ FPS in isolation; adds <2 ms per-frame.
For person crops (256x256), MiDaS Small generates a normalised monocular depth map. If depth variance < 0.005, crop is flagged as a flat-surface candidate (photo/screen). Calibrated: real
persons = 0.022–0.10, flat screens < 0.005. Runs at 200+ FPS in isolation; adds <5 ms. End-to-end cascade: 22–27 ms.

Thread-to-core affinity is pinned via os.sched_setaffinity, bounding scheduler jitter. The NPU inference thread (Core 1) and the secondary chain (Core 2) are decoupled by a bounded queue (capacity 2, non-blocking put_nowait; intentional drop when full). A separate frame_queue (depth 4, drop-if-full) decouples the NPU from web/alert services. Empirical result: 52.26 ± 0.76 FPS (n=709, CV=1.45%) across 6 modes under full concurrent load (SMTP, SSH clip upload, voice queries, MJPEG stream — 583 MB transferred).

Weapon-class detections increment a per-label consecutive-frame counter. Alert fires only when the counter reaches 3 without interruption — suppressing single-frame false positives while triggering within 3/52.2 ≈ 57.5 ms of a genuine threat. Weapon counters per class are independent.

FastAPI web server (Uvicorn, localhost:8080) exposed via Cloudflare Tunnel. Authentication: PBKDF2-SHA256 at 600,000 iterations, per-user salt, HTTP-only session cookie. Admin 2FA: 6-digit OTP via SMTPS, 10-minute expiry. ~45 REST routes with route-level role checks. Live-video: MJPEG, WebSocket binary, WebRTC (aiortc).
